claim.summary: For the literal r-by-r permutation-matrix CNF (O(r^3) literal length), its unique multilinear satisfaction indicator I_r is the sum of permutation point indicators, has degree<=r^2 and degree-r component perm_r (det_r in characteristic two). From a size-S depth-d circuit for I_r over k, interpolation at r^2+1 distinct elements of an extension E computes that component over E in size O((r^2+1)(S+r^2+1)), depth<=d+3. Over F2, E=F_(2^ceil(log2(r^2+1))) suffices; no binary-depth descent. In characteristic two I_r=det(M), M_ij=x_ij product_(k!=j)(1-x_ik).
claim.assessment: Working elementary indicator identity and costed interpolation, medium reviewed. Classical ingredients, novelty not claimed. Positive reduction changes field when needed; determinant-to-indicator substitution and the reverse interpolation are not an unqualified same-field equivalence.

claim.summary: There is no generic polynomial-size fixed-depth operation extracting arbitrary homogeneous components from all polynomial-size fixed-depth binary arithmetic circuits of polynomial degree. Already G_n=product(1+x_i), q=2^a, n=2q-1 has degree-q component e_q evaluating to majority, since binomial(w,q) mod2 is the a-th bit of w. Such an operation would contradict Smolensky's majority lower bound for AC0[2]. Binary constants and unbounded-fanin gates with wire size are essential.
claim.assessment: Working attributed elementary consequence of the published majority lower bound, medium reviewed. Does not rule out special component extraction with additional hypotheses or large-field interpolation.

claim.summary: Determinant polynomials over F2 have no polynomial-size fixed-depth arithmetic circuits with binary constants, by an explicit affine reduction of MOD3 to two determinants of order 2n+3 and addition of one. For A=[[0,1],[1,1]], M_i=I+x_i(A-I), the trace product detects weight not divisible by3; each diagonal entry is det([[T,b_u],[-c_u^T,0]]) for upper block-bidiagonal T with I_2 diagonal and -M_i superdiagonal. Thus universal cheap binary canonical extraction on padded permutation CNFs and cheap binary extraction of its degree-r component cannot both hold.
claim.assessment: Working explicit standard circuit-reduction consequence of Smolensky Theorem2, medium reviewed. No independent novelty. The conjunction obstruction does not identify which operation fails on the particular family; padded formulas themselves have cheap certificates. Extension constants excluded.

claim.summary: For any literal CNF satisfaction product H(x_1,...,x_r), append contradictory units on fresh z. Its satisfaction product P=-(z^2-z)H has explicit small constant-depth Boolean certificate Q=-H Z_z. Ordered monic division by B_1,...,B_r,B_z, passing each remainder onward, has final coefficient -ML(H). Thus universal efficient canonical-coefficient extraction even from supplied small certificates would efficiently multilinearize arbitrary CNF satisfaction products.
claim.assessment: Working explicit all-parameter projection, checked by same medium reviewer. A conditional complexity implication, not an unconditional hardness result. A difficult canonical coefficient does not imply certificate hardness, since these padded CNFs have explicit cheap certificates.

claim.summary: Smolensky's MOD3 lower bound implies a degree/descent scope gap: H_n=product_i(1+(zeta-1)x_i)+product_i(1+(zeta²-1)x_i), zeta²+zeta+1=0 over F4, is binary multilinear of degree<=n with O(n)-size depth<=4 unbounded-fan-in arithmetic circuits over F4, but has no polynomial-size fixed-depth F2 arithmetic circuits even agreeing on Boolean inputs. Its Boolean field relation has a degree-2n certificate. For n>=2, the satisfiable complete-map source {y-H_n,y²-y}, W=1,T=B=n,D=n² fits weighted degree descent but does not permit a fixed-depth polynomial-size binary map.
claim.assessment: Attributed scope corollary of Smolensky 1987 Theorem 2 and his root-of-unity construction. Degree/membership/rank descent remains valid. No new circuit lower-bound technique, hard CNF, general IPS certificate lower bound, or Frege lower bound is claimed.
